name: Ferroink Signal-Break Operative Set
description: This set leads with a structured moto-cut jacket in deep navy-black with an ink-wash ferrous brown panel running diagonally across the left chest and right shoulder — a deliberate asymmetry that makes the jacket memorable without being flashy. That visibility is a choice: this runner has a reputation and uses it. The jacket is single-layer reinforced with a Kevlar-analogue interlining that stops a blade and slows a low-caliber round without adding the bulk of obvious armor. The right sleeve is aug-cut — the outer seam from wrist to elbow opens on a ratchet-zip, accommodating full chrome arm augmentation with a secure reclose; when open, internal routing channels manage power and data cables cleanly along the forearm. Chest and inner-hem holster panels are built in, sized for compact sidearms or breaching tools. Beneath the jacket, a mandarin-collar shirt in dark teal shot-silk synthetic provides a layer of respectability — this outfit passes at a Tier 3 establishment without triggering dress-code scrutiny. The trousers are flat-front in deep charcoal with a subtle diamond-weave texture, cut to allow full-range leg movement and featuring a hidden inner-ankle holster channel on both legs. Footwear is a polished synthetic leather chelsea boot in dark brown, square-toe, with a reinforced steel toe cap concealed under the finish. A low-profile comm earpiece clips behind the ear with a near-invisible matte-black wire running under the collar.
functionality: Blade-resistant and low-caliber-resistant interlining; ratchet-zip aug-cut right sleeve for full chrome arm accommodation with cable routing; dual chest holster panels; inner-hem tool pockets; inner-ankle holster channels (bilateral); integrated comm earpiece routing under collar; passes Tier 3 dress code; reinforced steel toe footwear
what_it_says: This runner is good enough to be known and smart enough to still be careful. The jacket's diagonal colorblock is a signature — people in certain circles recognize it, and that's the point. The teal shirt and polished boots say this person can sit across from a Tier 3 client without embarrassing anyone. The steel toe says they've also kicked their way out of a situation before.
worn_by: operatives who trade on personal reputation
manufacturer: Ferroink — established street label, Circuit District, known quantity in runner communities
story_hooks: The jacket's diagonal colorblock is recognized mid-job by a target who knows exactly who the runner is — the element of surprise is gone, and now it's a negotiation or a fight.
A copycat runner is wearing a knockoff Ferroink jacket in the same colorblock, running a job that's about to go wrong — and witnesses are going to describe 'the Ferroink runner' to security.
A chrome-arm user's ratchet-zip seizes during a chase, locking the sleeve open and snagging on a door frame at the worst possible moment.
related_entities: TESSERA CORPONATION Aegis CorpSec Hardened Security BCI

physical_description.visual_profile: Sharp, asymmetrical runner's ensemble that reads professional-dangerous. The ferrous brown diagonal slash across navy-black creates deliberate visibility without ostentation. Silhouette is streamlined and combat-ready, with structured shoulders and a clean mandarin collar visible beneath. Overall impression: someone who has moved through violence and come out the other side with style.
physical_description.fit: Tailored but mobile. The jacket sits close at the torso with strategic articulation at shoulders and elbows. Trousers are slim through hip and thigh, widening slightly at ankle for boot clearance. Allows full range of motion without excess fabric.
physical_description.primary_material: Jacket: reinforced synth-wool with Kevlar-analogue interlining. Mandarin shirt: dark teal shot-silk synthetic. Trousers: treated composite weave. Boots: polished synthetic leather with concealed steel.
physical_description.texture: Jacket surface is smooth with a subtle sheen from the wash treatment. Ferrous brown panel has a matte, oxidized quality. Trousers feature fine diamond-weave visible under direct light. Boot leather appears supple and deliberately buffed.
physical_description.color_scheme: Deep navy-black dominant. Ferrous brown diagonal accent running chest to shoulder. Dark teal mandarin shirt visible at neck. Charcoal trousers. Dark brown boots. All colors muted, urban, non-reflective.
physical_description.closures: Jacket: standard buttons with magnetic snap reinforcement. Right sleeve: ratchet-zip aug-accommodation. Mandarin shirt: concealed magnetic closures. Trousers: friction-fit waistband with hidden security snap. Boots: Chelsea-style elastic side panels.
distinctive_features: Asymmetrical ferrous brown diagonal panel signaling reputation/status
Aug-cut right sleeve with ratchet-zip for chrome arm accommodation
Internal routing channels for power/data cable management
Chest and inner-hem holster panels for compact sidearms
Hidden inner-ankle holster channels on both pant legs
Concealed steel toe cap under boot finish
Low-profile matte-black comm earpiece with near-invisible collar wire
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3 functional-professional with Tier 2 craftsmanship. Ferroink is street-established; this set costs Φ800-1200, accessible to working runners but signals investment in serious equipment.
physical_description.cultural_context: Runner/operative culture. Someone with a reputation who moves through corpo spaces without triggering red flags. The asymmetry is a calling card—this person wants their work known. Medical/law enforcement adjacent aesthetic without being either.
physical_description.condition_typical: Worn in but meticulously maintained. The ferrous brown panel shows subtle darkening from sweat and city grime. Jacket seams are crisp. Boots are regularly polished. Holster panels show minimal creasing—equipment passes through cleanly. No visible patching; this is active maintenance, not salvage.
